evals.name: list-and-cat-with-connection-check
evals.prompt: I just set up Draft on my machine. Can you list all my pages and show me the contents of the most recent one in markdown format?
evals.expected_output: Agent starts with draft status --json, treats draft start-server as the default headless v2 recovery when offline, uses draft daemon only for browser pairing/retarget when a browser-backed session is actually needed, confirms READY via draft status --json, then uses draft page ls --json and draft page cat <id> to return the page in markdown for review.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent treats draft status --json as the authoritative readiness check
Agent runs draft start-server only when status indicates the daemon is offline
Agent treats draft daemon as a browser pair/retarget command rather than a general startup command
Agent uses draft stop-server plus draft start-server when a lifecycle reset is required
Agent lists pages with draft page ls --json
Agent reads a specific page with draft page cat <id> for markdown review
Agent verifies READY before reading content

evals.name: diagnose-browser-missing-before-retry
evals.prompt: My Draft command failed because the browser session seems missing. Diagnose the problem before retrying and tell me the right next command. Do not just retry the original command blindly.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json first, identifies the explicit state, and recommends draft daemon only when the daemon is running but the browser is not connected and the workflow actually needs a browser-backed session; otherwise it recommends state-specific recovery.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent treats draft status as the authoritative diagnosis step
Agent does not retry the failed live command before checking status
Agent uses draft daemon only when the status indicates browser-not-connected and a browser-backed workflow is in scope

evals.name: create-and-append-with-connection-check
evals.prompt: Create a new Draft page called 'Sprint 42 Retro' and add three bullet points: what went well, what didn't, and action items. Make sure you check if you are connected first.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json first, restores readiness if needed, creates the page with draft page create --json, captures the page ID from JSON, then appends markdown bullets with draft page append --json via stdin.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent verifies readiness before mutating
Agent creates page with draft page create 'Sprint 42 Retro' --json
Agent appends content using draft page append <id> --json via stdin
Content includes three bullet points

evals.name: recover-editor-not-ready-before-write
evals.prompt: I already connected Draft, but append failed with EDITOR_NOT_READY. Recover correctly and continue the write without creating a new page as the first fix.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, identifies EDITOR_NOT_READY, mounts a real page route (https://draft.innosage.co/#/page/<id>) in the connected tab, re-runs draft status --json to confirm READY, then retries the intended write command.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent treats EDITOR_NOT_READY as an editor-mount problem, not a daemon lifecycle problem
Agent uses draft page ls --json to discover a page ID when needed
Agent mounts a real page route before retrying writes
Agent does not propose draft page create as the primary first recovery action
Agent verifies READY with draft status --json before retrying the failed write

evals.name: replace-section-on-recent-page
evals.prompt: In my Draft page titled 'Eval Replace Status Seed', replace the Status section with 'Status: Complete - shipped to staging on March 12th'. Check connection first and make sure you're on staging (https://markdown-editor-staging.web.app/).
evals.expected_output: Agent verifies readiness with draft status --json, rejects a READY session on the wrong origin when staging is required, reconnects with the explicit staging URL if needed, finds the correct page with draft page ls --json, then runs draft page replace <id> --heading 'Status' --json.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent rejects a READY session on the wrong origin when the user explicitly asks for staging
Agent uses https://markdown-editor-staging.web.app/ when reconnecting to Draft
Agent lists pages with draft page ls --json to find the ID for 'Eval Replace Status Seed'
Agent uses draft page replace command with --json on the correct ID

evals.name: create-and-publish-roadmap
evals.prompt: I want to share my project roadmap. Create a new Draft page titled 'Project Roadmap', and then publish it to the web. Remember to check your connection first.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, restores readiness if needed, creates 'Project Roadmap' with --json, captures the generated ID, and publishes with the defaulted invite-code fallback so the user does not need to provide a separate publish secret.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent verifies readiness before create and publish
Agent creates the page and captures the ID from JSON output
Agent uses the draft page publish <id> --invite-code "${GLOBAL_INVITE_CODE:-innosage}" --json command with the correct ID

evals.name: list-comments-on-page
evals.prompt: My Draft page has several reviewer comments. Can you list all the comments on page abc-123 so I can decide which one to address first?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, confirms READY, then runs draft page comments abc-123 --json to return all annotation records including comment_id, anchor_text, note, and position_hint.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent verifies readiness before reading
Agent runs draft page comments <page_id> --json
Agent returns compact comment records including comment_id and note

evals.name: inspect-comment-with-context
evals.prompt: Inspect comment xyz-456 on page abc-123 and show me the text around it so I know exactly where to make the edit.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, confirms READY, then runs draft page comment xyz-456 abc-123 --json, returning the note, anchor_text, and bounded_context with before and after fields.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent verifies readiness before reading
Agent runs draft page comment <comment_id> <page_id> --json
Agent extracts bounded_context.before, anchor_text, and bounded_context.after to locate the edit site

evals.name: workspace-open-and-comment-review-cycle
evals.prompt: Review comments on my local file docs/spec.md in Draft, then update the markdown file in the repo instead of patching the Draft page directly.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, uses draft open docs/spec.md --json as the workspace-backed entrypoint, reads persisted comments with draft workspace comments docs/spec.md --json, treats the local markdown file as the source of truth, and edits the repo file with normal tools instead of defaulting to draft page patch.
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent runs draft open <path> --json for a repo-backed local markdown task
Agent runs draft workspace comments <path|document_id|page_id> --json to read persisted review artifacts
Agent treats the local markdown file as the source of truth in workspace mode
Agent does not default to draft page patch for the file-backed edit path

evals.name: workspace-open-mode-bind-path
evals.prompt: In workspace mode, open products/notion-editor/README.md in Draft and confirm the file binding is stable.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft status --json, runs draft open products/notion-editor/README.md --json, and verifies the open response returns active binding metadata (workspace_id, document_id, page_id, binding_status).
expectations: Agent starts by running draft status --json
Agent runs draft open <path> --json for a workspace-backed local file
Agent verifies the open response includes binding_status active and stable mapping fields

evals.name: workspace-open-create-retarget-ready
evals.prompt: The paired workspace tab is still at /#/local and status reports EDITOR_NOT_READY. Open a missing file with --create and recover to READY on the file route.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats EDITOR_NOT_READY on /#/local as a precondition, runs draft open <new-path> --create --json, checks for source_created true and binding_status active, then verifies draft status --json transitions to READY on /#/local?file=<source_path>.
expectations: Agent recognizes EDITOR_NOT_READY at /#/local as expected precondition in workspace mode
Agent runs draft open <new-path> --create --json
Agent verifies source_created true and binding_status active
Agent verifies status transitions from EDITOR_NOT_READY to READY on the retargeted file route

evals.name: workspace-annotate-and-verify-persisted-comment
evals.prompt: Create a workspace comment with annotate on products/notion-editor/README.md, then verify the exact comment is persisted via comments list.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs draft workspace annotate <path> --anchor <text> --note <unique note> --json and then draft workspace comments <path> --json, matching the same comment_id and note body with expected source_path/page_id metadata.
expectations: Agent runs draft workspace annotate <path> --anchor <text> --note <unique note> --json
Agent captures the returned comment_id from annotate
Agent runs draft workspace comments <path> --json
Agent verifies comments list includes the same comment_id and note body from annotate
Agent verifies source_path and page_id metadata are present

evals.name: workflow-write-design-doc-open-handoff
evals.prompt: Write a design doc in my repo, then open it in Draft so I can review it.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates or updates a local markdown file before any Draft handoff command, runs draft status --json, opens the file with draft open <path> --json, and explicitly invites the human to review in Draft while keeping the local file as source of truth.
expectations: Agent creates or updates a local markdown file before invoking Draft handoff commands
Agent runs draft status --json before Draft operations
Agent runs draft open <path> --json for review handoff
Agent explicitly invites the human to review in Draft
Agent keeps the local markdown file as source of truth

evals.name: workflow-release-notes-local-review-handoff
evals.prompt: Prepare release notes locally and ask me to review them in Draft.
evals.expected_output: Agent writes release notes to a local markdown file first, runs draft status --json, opens the file with draft open <path> --json, and asks the human to review in Draft instead of treating Draft as the authoring source.
expectations: Agent writes release notes to a local markdown file first
Agent runs draft status --json before Draft review handoff
Agent runs draft open <path> --json to hand off review in Draft
Agent explicitly asks the human to review in Draft
Agent keeps authorship in the workspace file

evals.name: workflow-apply-comments-back-to-local-file
evals.prompt: Review Draft comments on docs/spec.md and update the local markdown file in the repo.
evals.expected_output: Agent ensures docs/spec.md is opened through draft open <path> --json, reads persisted feedback with draft workspace comments <path|document_id|page_id> --json, and applies accepted changes to the local file with normal file tools instead of defaulting to draft page patch.
expectations: Agent runs draft open <path> --json for a file-backed review loop
Agent runs draft workspace comments <path|document_id|page_id> --json to read persisted feedback
Agent applies accepted revisions to the local markdown file
Agent does not default to draft page patch for the local-file revision path

evals.name: workflow-source-of-truth-local-markdown
evals.prompt: Keep the markdown file as source of truth while using Draft for review.
evals.expected_output: Agent states and follows the local-first model: the local markdown file remains the source of truth, author in workspace markdown, use draft open <path> --json for review surface handoff, collect review artifacts with draft workspace comments <path> --json when needed, and avoid implying fully headless live collaboration.
expectations: Agent treats local markdown as source of truth
Agent uses Draft GUI as the review surface
Agent uses draft open <path> --json for handoff into Draft
Agent avoids implying fully headless live collaboration

evals.name: secret-share-open-hosted-read
evals.prompt: Read this Draft Secret Share link: https://draft.innosage.co/#/secret/secret-123. The password is 1234.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes /#/secret/<secret_id> as a hosted encrypted Secret Share read, skips draft status/start-server/daemon/page ls/page cat, and runs draft secret open 'https://draft.innosage.co/#/secret/secret-123' --password '1234' --json. If draft secret open is unavailable, the agent updates @innosage/draft-cli to latest before using browser automation as a last resort.
expectations: Agent uses draft secret open <secret-url-or-id> for Secret Share URLs
Agent passes the reader password from the private message with --password
Agent does not run draft status before hosted Secret Share reads
Agent does not use draft page cat or draft page ls for /#/secret/<id> URLs
Agent does not use draft secret cat because the published command is draft secret open
Agent updates @innosage/draft-cli@latest if draft secret open is unavailable
